attorneys.name: Jason Mcleod Kidder
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Violence Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
My name is Jason McLeod Kidder, and I am a highly respected Criminal Defense Attorney based in Little Rock, Arkansas. I am the proud owner of Kidder Criminal Defense, which I opened to serve the People of Arkansas and anyone facing criminal charges in the State of Arkansas.

My passion for Criminal Defense was born in my first year of law school when I had my eyes opened to the numerous injustices, unfairness, and major flaws in the criminal justice system. I immediately began gaining hands on experience defending clients while working directly under one of Arkansas’s top criminal defense lawyers, while simultaneously attending law school.

My sole focus and only practice area of law is in criminal defense. I have an immense passion for criminal defense and I have been highly successful in defending Driving While Intoxicated/Driving while Under the Influence (DWI/DUI), drug possession, drug trafficking, and domestic violence cases

I am a native of Little Rock, Arkansas and before attending Law School, I attended the University of Central Arkansas in Conway where I earned my Bachelor’s Degree in Finance and graduated with magna cum laude honors. After graduation I was faced with the dilemma of either going straight to work or continuing down the pathway of education. Naturally, I chose to continue my education and earned an academic scholarship to the William H. Bowen School of Law in the heart of Downtown Little Rock. I graduated from the Bowen School of Law with magna cum laude honors in addition to working full-time and being a full-time father and husband.

I made the decision to step away from a top Arkansas criminal defense firm to open Kidder Criminal Defense in January of 2025. This decision came with one only goal in mind: To be the best law firm for my clients rather than the biggest. I bring years of experience working State cases, such as simple traffic violations, to Federal Cases, such as complex murder cases, and everything else in between to Kidder Criminal Defense.

My approach to representing my clients is very simple: every case is different, every client is unique and important, and every one of my clients deserves the best defense tailored to meet their specific needs and goals. The Prosecution will never, ever outwork me. I will go through every piece of evidence with a magnifying glass and fine-tooth comb, and no stone will be left unturned when it comes to defending my clients from the government and justice system. Above all, I want you to be able to make informed decisions about your future. My goal is to get the best possible outcome, but only you can tell me what is best and most important to you.

When I am not in the office or in the courtroom, I am a dedicated husband and father of two beautiful children. My family is a source of inspiration and motivation for me, but most importantly they serve as a reminder of what is at stake and on the line for my clients and their own families and loved ones.

When your rights, freedom, and future are on the line, trust an attorney who will stand by your side and fight tirelessly for you. When you need serious help, call Kidder Criminal Defense.

attorneys.name: Patrick Lee
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Patrick Lee has lived in central Arkansas all his life, and is proud to call it home. Lee was born and raised in Little Rock where he graduated from Little Rock Central High in 2007. Lee studied sociology at Hendrix College in Conway where he developed a deep-seated desire to serve his community. During his studies at Hendrix, he served as a resident assistant in Hardin Hall and also volunteered at the Heifer Ranch in Perryville, working on the ropes course and teaching leadership seminars. Lee’s studies in sociology taught him about the hardships faced by working American families, and he decided then and there he would devote his career to helping people any way he could.

Following his graduation from Hendrix College, Lee worked as an AmeriCorps member tutoring third graders in struggling Little Rock elementary schools in math and literacy.

His drive to serve working families eventually led him to return to school to get his law degree. In the fall of 2015, Lee enrolled in the William H. Bowen School of Law. During law school, Lee clerked for a prominent Little Rock criminal defense attorney and for a circuit judge in Pulaski County.

After graduating, Lee took an associate position at Wilson & Haubert, where he served clients with family law and probate matters.

Hoping to better assist needy families, he took a position as a pro bono attorney at the Center for Arkansas Legal Services. At CALS, Lee practiced in the areas of criminal record sealing and VA disability compensation appeals.

Lee found his home at Rainwater, Holt, & Sexton in August 2020, where he now works as a personal injury attorney fighting insurance companies to ensure injured Arkansans are justly compensated for their injuries by the negligent parties who hurt them.

When he is not defending his clients’ interests, Lee enjoys tennis, reading, and spending time with his wife, Liz, and their three children: Nora, Margot, and Eli.

attorneys.name: Nathan Daniel Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relations/Family Law Lawyers in Cabot, AR
attorneys.bio:
I was born in Reno, Nevada on July 17, 1983. My parents divorced when I was 3, so I have experienced the turmoil between divorcing partners from a very early age. I eventually decided that it was best for me to live with my father, so I moved to Heber Springs, Arkanas when I was 12 and have remained in Arkansas since. I attented Heber Springs High School and graduated in 2001, before moving to Jonesboro, Arkansas to attend college at Arkansas State University. In 2009, I graduated from Arkansas State University with a Bachelor of Science in Sports Management and minors in Business Management and Marketing. I earned my Juris Doctorate from the William Bowen School of Law in Little Rock in 2013, where I graduated with Honors. During law school, I clerked for three years at the Arkansas State Supreme Court Office of the Clerk.

In addition to being an Arkansas licensed attorney, I am currently a member of the Arkansas Army National Guard, and have served since August of 2004. I have held multiple different positions in the military as both an enlisted Soldier and a Commissioned Officer. I have held the Military Occupational Specialties of a Legal Specialist and Signal Support Specialists as an enlisted Soldier, and served as an Intelligence Officer and Maintenance Officer while a Commissioned Officer. I am a veteran and have been deployed to Iraq in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom from July 2006 to October 2007.

I have a wonderful family and am married to my beautiful wife, Bridget, and we have two sons, Aaden Jack and William Daniel (Liam). When not practicing law, my interests include activities with my family, coaching my sons baseball teams, sports, exercise, and running.

attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in North Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Doug Lickert is an attorney and certified public accountant (CPA) with more than 25 years of combined legal and business experience. His primary areas of practice include bankruptcy, divorce, estate planning, and business law. Mr. Lickert received a Masters of Business Administration from W. Texas A&M University and a Juris Doctorate from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock School of Law. He is a member of the Arkansas Bar Association, Arkansas Trial Lawyers Association, and the National Association of Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys. Mr. Lickert has served as an adjunct instructor at Pulaski Technical College and as a speaker for seminars conducted by the National Business Institute.

Prior to becoming an attorney, Mr. Lickert served as a Vice President of a financial services firm and worked as a commercial loan officer and loan workout specialist with a large commercial bank. He has audited small to medium sized businesses as a CPA for certified public accountant firms in Atlanta, Georgia, and Little Rock, Arkansas.

Mr. Lickert has a passion for helping individuals and small businesses facing financial difficulties, and is uniquely qualified to provide superior services to those individuals and small businesses. He offers free consultations for debt related problems, including bankruptcy. Unlike many large bankruptcy firms, Mr. Lickert is personally involved in every phase of the bankruptcy process for all of his clients, including meeting with his clients, preparing information for the bankruptcy petition and schedules, attending meetings and hearings, and personally answering any questions that clients might have. He monitors the case from start to finish to ensure that each client obtains the relief he or she is seeking.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Jake Logan was born and raised in Sheridan, Arkansas where he attended high school and graduated co-valedictorian. During his sophomore year at the University of Central Arkansas, he knew he wanted to pursue a career in law. It would be a lifelong pursuit to understand the rules, argue their influence and use them to help clients. He graduated from UCA in 2013 magna cum laude.

He attended the University of Arkansas at Little Rock Bowen School of Law where he was an Associate Editor on the Law Review and was also on the Moot Court Board. He graduated magna cum laude from law school in 2016 and passed the Arkansas Bar in July 2016. He passed the Missouri Uniform Bar Exam in February 2018 and is licensed to practice law in Missouri as well. His growing litigation and trial experience gave him the ability to educate and advise his clients on the merits of each case thoroughly.

After law school, Jake stayed in Little Rock with his wife, Mary, and their two adopted dogs, Chief and Ruby. He is active in community organizations and holds a position within his church, St. Margaret’s Episcopal Church. He is also active in the Rotaract Club of Little Rock, the Hat Club of Little Rock, and Create Little Rock. Jake is also a member of the legal organization of the Judge William R. Overton Inn of Court.

At Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, he practices injury litigation of all types but has an emphasis on premise liability cases where his clients are injured by the negligence of a store or business owner. He looks forward to helping you pursue recovery from your injury.

attorneys.name: Ashley Loy
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Ashley Loy was born and raised in Arkansas. She always had a passion for standing up for others who needed help, and she felt that passion could best be served by becoming an attorney and truly advocating for those who need assistance. While enrolled in the night program at William H. Bowen School of Law, Ashley worked as an adjudicator for Social Security Administration’s Disability Determination Services (DDS). She became intimately familiar with Social Security’s rules and regulations and how the Administration decided who was eligible for benefits. After working for DDS for over five years, she learned how the decision-making process could sometimes play out unfairly for many people who deserved benefits.

After graduating from law school with honors, Ashley immediately went to work with Rainwater, Holt & Sexton. She wanted to use her years of knowledge and experience of how the Social Security Administration handles disability claims to effectively advocate for people who had their benefits denied. Rainwater, Holt & Sexton’s reputation for being fierce advocates for their clients grabbed Ashley’s attention, and she knew she wanted to be a part of that team. She treats every case on an individual basis, recognizing the facts that make each case, and each client, unique. She makes understanding each client’s circumstances a priority so that she can formulate the best strategy for that client’s case.

Like handling a claim for benefits from a big government, Ashley also recognizes the challenges in obtaining resolution and justice from big insurance companies after an accident. It’s not always easy being the David going up against the Goliath, whether that means the government or a big insurance company, but when you have a dedicated, diligent, and determined attorney at your side you also have the confidence that comes with working with the Rainwater, Holt & Sexton team.

attorneys.name: Jeremy McNabb
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Jeremy McNabb is a native Arkansan born and raised in Pocahontas, Arkansas. Jeremy graduated from Pocahontas High School and then attended the University of Arkansas at Fayetteville, where he earned a degree in business finance. During his time in college, he decided to pursue a legal career. Jeremy moved to Little Rock to begin his studies at the William H. Bowen School of Law at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock. Jeremy is licensed to practice law in Arkansas, Tennessee, and Missouri.

Immediately after law school, Jeremy practiced criminal law for the State of Arkansas and learned how to navigate a courtroom. Jeremy then went to work as an associate attorney for the attorneys who later founded Rainwater, Holt & Sexton. “I have been fortunate enough to be with Rainwater, Holt & Sexton from the very beginning. It has been exciting to be a part of a team that has grown to be the largest personal injury law firm in Arkansas,” he said.

While growing up in the McNabb home, Jeremy recalls his family continually instructing and putting into practice two essential life principles: First, always give your best effort in everything you do. Second, a full life is one lived in the service of others. Whatever it is—raising a family, working on relationships, practicing his faith, working—he works hard to implement both of those principles.

At Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, Jeremy serves clients in numerous practice areas, including representing county officials in the county defense practice, helping start and grow the Social Security Disability practice, and representing clients who have suffered significant personal injuries. Jeremy considers it a privilege to come to work each day and represent the great people of Arkansas. “For me, it always comes back to those two essential life principles. We represent people with complicated legal issues and that requires nothing less than my best effort all of the time. And, I want each of my clients to know that my representation of them is of the highest priority and that their interest always, and I mean always, comes before mine,” Jeremy said.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Super Lawyers® Rising Star, 2011

attorneys.name: Meredith Moore
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Meredith Moore was born and raised in Memphis, Tennessee, but came to Arkansas to study at Hendrix College. After completing her undergraduate degree, Meredith moved to Little Rock to attend law school at the Bowen School of Law. While in law school, she clerked for a Pulaski County Circuit Court Judge for four years and was an Associate Editor for the school’s Law Review. From there, she went on to work as a prosecuting attorney for the Pulaski County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office, primarily prosecuting Felony domestic violence, child abuse, and sexual assault cases.

After three years of working as a prosecuting attorney and gaining invaluable litigation experience, Meredith decided to make the transition into civil law. She chose personal injury law to represent those who have been victims of negligence and reckless behavior.

“I knew Rainwater, Holt & Sexton was the firm for me because of their serious dedication to helping their clients at times in their lives when they need it most,” Meredith said. Giving individualized attention to each of her clients and their cases is Meredith’s primary goal to ensure the best end result, whether that be settlement or litigation.

Meredith loves living and working in Arkansas and enjoys being involved in the community. She is on the House of Delegates for the Arkansas Bar Association, a member of the Pulaski County Bar Association, the Arkansas Trial Lawyers Association, and the Arkansas Association of Women Lawyers. She also enjoys volunteering for the Central Arkansas Boys and Girls Club.

“I make it a priority to get to know my clients just as much as I get to know their case. Understanding each person, the facts of the case, and how he or she has been affected by another’s wrongdoing is my approach to effectively representing my clients.”

After receiving his undergraduate degree in Business Finance from the University of Arkansas, Morgan returned to Little Rock where he received his Juris Doctorate from the Bowen School of Law.

After law school, Morgan served as a judicial law clerk for Pulaski County Circuit Court Judge Tim Fox before going to work as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney for the Pulaski County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office. During his time as a Prosecuting Attorney, he advocated for victims of Pulaski County and litigated a wide range of felony cases.

Morgan realizes the importance of giving every client he works with the required attention they deserve in order to achieve a resolution that is fair for them. He will be a trusted advisor and advocate for those who entrust him as their attorney. His drive to help others who have fallen victim to circumstances through no fault of their own is what brought him to Rainwater, Holt & Sexton.

In his free time, Morgan enjoys playing golf, rooting on the Razorbacks, and spending time with his wife, son, and their two Irish Terriers. He is a member of the Arkansas Bar Association and the Pulaski County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Chris Oswalt
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
As a father of two young children, I am a firm believer that both parents have a fundamental right to have a meaningful and lasting role in our children's development. More importantly, however, and especially applicable to the practice of family law, the best interests of our children must always take precedent. At Robertson, Oswalt, Nony & Kennedy PLLC, I use my life experiences and legal experiences, to guide my clients through the intricate and unpredictable nature of a modern-day family law case.

Further, as the fundamental right to maintain and grow familial relationships does not end at death, I believe it is imperative to establish a proper plan for the distribution of one's assets after their passing, in order to provide protection, assurance, and comfort to loved ones left behind. Whether by a simple will or more complex estate planning, I assist my clients in making sure their assets are distributed by the method they desire and to the people they choose.

attorneys.name: David W. Parker
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Former prosecutor, David Parker, joined Dodds, Kidd, Ryan & Rowan in 2017. After graduating from UALR William H. Bowen School of Law in 2008, David worked as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney, where he prosecuted over 30,000 criminal cases in White County District and Circuit Courts. There, he also served as Special Judge in White County District Court – Civil Division.

Following his time as a prosecutor, David worked at the Department of Finance and Administration as Revenue Legal Counsel. There, David represented the department in all DWI drivers’ license appeal cases for the entire state of Arkansas. As part of his representation for the department, David played a key role in lobbying legislators and drafting legislation regarding Arkansas’ DWI laws, licensing and criminal statutes. Besides his work on DWI appeals, David litigated tax protests, business closures, and other civil lawsuits on behalf of DFA.

As a Little Rock native, David serves on the Board of Directors for the Big Dam Bridge Foundation, whose mission is to promote the use, support, and preservation of the Big Dam Bridge for the advancement of health, fitness, cultural and recreational activities in Arkansas. David is also among the sixteen founding members of the Little Rock Touchdown Club, where membership has grown to more than 800 members, with the purpose of bringing football fans together to support all levels of Arkansas football.

attorneys.name: Madison Parks
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Madison Parks was born in Little Rock, Arkansas, and grew up in Greenville, Mississippi. While she loved her time in the Mississippi Delta, she was excited to return to her home state of Arkansas for her undergraduate education. She graduated from Ouachita Baptist University with a degree in Business Management and Marketing. While at Ouachita, her business professors planted a seed in her brain that got her interested in the practice of law. Fully running with this new legal interest, she became president of Ouachita’s Pre-Law Society. After graduating from Ouachita, she attended the University of Arkansas William H. Bowen School of Law.

Parks was drawn to the legal field because she knew she wanted to find a career that interested and challenged her, while allowing her the opportunity to help people every day. While in law school, Parks developed her admiration for helping clients through Bowen’s Business Innovations Clinic. It was through working with clients in the clinic that she decided that using her legal career to positively impact individuals’ lives was her ultimate goal.

Upon law school graduation and admission to the Arkansas State Bar, Parks said she was drawn to the enthusiasm and kindness that Rainwater, Holt, & Sexton displayed when advocating for their clients, as well as through their continuous involvement in our community. She joined Rainwater, Holt & Sexton in 2022 and looks forward to continuing the firm’s devotion to bettering our clients and our community.

In her free time, Parks enjoys spending time with her friends and family, boating on Lake Hamilton in Hot Springs, attending concerts, and traveling to explore all of the fun and beautiful places Arkansas has to offer.

attorneys.name: Jeff Priebe
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Priebe is a native Arkansan born and raised in Mountain Home, Arkansas. After graduating from Mountain Home High School, he received a Bachelor of Science degree in Agriculture Business in 1998 and a Juris Doctorate in 2001, both from the University of Arkansas at Fayetteville.

After passing the bar exam in 2001, he served as an Assistant Attorney General under then-Attorney General’s Mark Pryor and Mike Beebe. After his tenure at the Attorney General’s office, he became an in-house attorney to retired General Wesley Clark’s 2004 Presidential Campaign. He has practiced at national law firms including Armstrong Allen and Wilkes & McHugh. He later joined and was a partner with James, Carter, and Priebe law firm. At Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, Priebe works on nursing home litigation, representing those who have been mistreated by the nursing home industry. He also has experience in election law and other personal injury litigation.

In 2010, Priebe had the honor of being appointed by Governor Mike Beebe to serve as a Special Justice on the Arkansas Supreme Court. He also teaches election law as an adjunct professor at the UALR Law School.

Priebe is licensed to practice law in Arkansas, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Missouri, Illinois, Kentucky, and before the United States Supreme Court. In addition, he is a member of the Arkansas Bar Association, a Board Member of the Arkansas Trial Lawyers Association, and participates in various other legal organizations.

attorneys.name: Mike Rainwater
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Born in Little Rock, Mike Rainwater’s family roots go back to Crawford and White County. Mike graduated from North Little Rock High School and attended college at Henderson State University and Louisiana Tech. After college, Mike lived and worked in Colorado, Louisiana, and Texas. Mike is licensed to practice law in Arkansas, Tennessee, and Mississippi.

In 1973, Mike joined Texas Eastern Corporation as a computer programmer, working in Shreveport. “When I was working as a computer programmer fresh out of college, I realized that I liked to talk to people more than computers,” he said. “This was in the early 1970s when there was a lot of social unrest and I developed a desire to go to law school.”

He knew if he didn’t attend, he would regret it the rest of his life. He soon enrolled in South Texas College of Law in Houston. As it turned out, Mike loved the law and loved law school. He continued to work for Texas Eastern Corporation during the day while taking law school classes at night.

Upon graduation, Mike moved back to Arkansas with his wife to practice law and start a family. Mike worked as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Little Rock and built relationships with local judges, court personnel, and lawyers. He then moved on to a private practice and learned about commercial law, including bankruptcy. During this time, he learned about commercial transactions and built relationships with many of the commercial entities in Central Arkansas.

Mike then joined Little Rock attorney John Gill at his new law firm, a spin-off from the Mitchell Law Firm. Gill hired Mike to represent Arkansas’ city officials through the Arkansas Municipal League Defense Fund Program, one of Gill’s long-term clients. Mike worked with city officials all over Arkansas and fell in love with constitutional law.

In 1985, he approached the Association of Arkansas Counties with the idea of forming its own liability defense program for Arkansas’ counties. That program started in 1987, and Mike and his law firm served as litigation counsel for the Association of Arkansas Counties. He represented county officials for 31 years was involved in over 6,000 cases. He is still Outside General Counsel to the AAC Risk Management Fund.

In 1993, Mike formed his own law firm to tackle the plaintiff’s personal injury practice. He joined Little Rock personal injury lawyer Phillip Duncan and for the next 13 years he and Duncan worked together as personal injury lawyers on catastrophic injury cases.

“I feel called to help individuals who are hurting from injury or other situations that have them on the sidelines of life,” Mike said. “I really enjoy building relationships. I love when the representation ends with a fully satisfied client and we have made a difference in someone’s life.”

On January 1, 2006, Mike, Stephen Holt, and Bob Sexton formed Rainwater, Holt & Sexton. Today, Rainwater, Holt and Sexton is over 25 lawyers strong. Unfortunately, Stephen Holt passed away in 2014 from ALS. The firm name remains Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, with the Holt name being retained as a tribute to Mike and Bob’s beloved law partner, Stephen Holt.

What began as only a handful of lawyers has now grown to over 25 attorneys and over 100 support staff. The growth, according to Mike, is because of the care and compassion shown to each client.

“Everything we do is all about putting clients first,” Mike said. “That is the foundation of the firm. We know if we put our clients first, then everything else will take care of itself.”

Mike calls all of Arkansas “home.” He has represented cities, counties, and over 30,000 of Arkansas’ citizens – all over the state. He wants to be there for injured people and their families and strives to care for his fellow Arkansans.

“At Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, we are all in this together,” Mike said. “We are grateful to be able to come alongside and support our neighbors when they are facing a dark or difficult situation.”

Mike and his wife enjoy spending time with three sons and daughters in law and their six grandchildren. When he needs to get away, you can often find him hard at work on the family farm in Clark County, fishing on the Little Red River in Cleburne County or duck hunting in Arkansas County.

What began as only a handful of lawyers has now grown to over 25 attorneys and over 100 support staff. The growth, according to Mike, is because of the care and compassion shown to each client.

“Everything we do is all about putting clients first,” Mike said. “That is the foundation of the firm. We know if we put our clients first, then everything else will take care of itself.”

Mike calls all of Arkansas “home.” He has represented cities, counties, and over 30,000 of Arkansas’ citizens – all over the state. He wants to be there for injured people and their families and strives to care for his fellow Arkansans.

“At Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, we are all in this together,” Mike said. “We are grateful to be able to come alongside and support our neighbors when they are facing a dark or difficult situation.”

Mike and his wife enjoy spending time with three sons and daughters in law and their six grandchildren. When he needs to get away, you can often find him hard at work on the family farm in Clark County, fishing on the Little Red River in Cleburne County or duck hunting in Arkansas County.

attorneys.name: John M. Rainwater
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
John Rainwater has been practicing law in Arkansas since 2009. While he is primarily focused on his personal injury practice, he has also represented debtors in Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcy cases, handled disability cases, litigated class action cases against multi-million-dollar companies, and defended law enforcement officers in Section 1983 cases. He litigates cases in federal and state courts and has also tried cases in front of the Arkansas Claims Commission.

After completing his Juris Doctorate at the University of Arkansas School of Law in Little Rock, Arkansas, John was admitted as a member to the Arkansas Bar in 2009. He was also admitted to practice before the U.S. District Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Arkansas in 2009. and practiced before the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Arkansas in 2011.

Before becoming an attorney, John earned his B.S.B.A. in Accountancy from the Sam Walton School of Business at the University of Arkansas in 2005. John’s accounting degree trained him to think practically, efficiently, and logically, allowing him to be a better advocate for his clients. He puts this education and experience to work every day in serving his clients’ interests.

John is a board member of the Volunteers’ Organization Center for Arkansas Legal Services (VOCALS) and is a board member of the Alumni Association of the William H. Bowen School of Law. He was a member of the House of Delegates of the Arkansas Bar Association from 2015-2018, served on several different committees of the Arkansas Bar Association, and was a member of the Executive Council of the Young Lawyers’ Section of the Arkansas Bar Association from 2014-2018. He was the treasurer, vice-president, and president of the Debtor-Creditor Bar of Central Arkansas from 2014-2017. He is an active member of Immanuel Baptist Church and has coached Little League baseball at Junior Deputy since 2015.

John was recognized as one of the Best Lawyers in Little Rock for Bankruptcy in 2015, 2016, and 2017. He was also recognized and distinguished by the “National Trial Lawyers” and “Top 100 Trial Lawyers.” He was presented with Awards of Excellence from the Arkansas Bar Association Young Lawyers’ Section in 2014-2017, and was the Judith Ryan Gray Outstanding Young Lawyer Service Award recipient in 2017. John has been a frequent speaker at continuing legal education seminars, including the Annual Arkansas Debtor/Creditor Law Institute and the National Association of Chapter 13 Trustees Annual Meeting.

John is deeply devoted to helping people who have been hurt, harmed, or otherwise challenged by the legal system. His ability to understand and empathize with his clients makes him a very successful and effective advocate. John currently lives in Little Rock with his wife, daughter, and two sons. John loves being a dad and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Brian D. Reddick
attorneys.practice_type: Personal & Catastrophic Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Brian Reddick is a fifth - generation Arkansan who has successfully delivered big verdicts, big settlements in big cases for almost 30 years. Mr. Reddick has mostly focused his national practice on cases involving catastrophic injuries, wrongful death, fraud, trucking accidents, class actions, mass torts and nursing home negligence. Trying his first jury trial one year out of law school as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Pulaski County on behalf of a victim whose life was destroyed by violent crime, ignited a passion to help people who have been harmed. Today, Mr. Reddick is the founder of a national law firm with offices in multiple states serving hundreds of clients across the country.

Despite Reddick Law PLLC's national profile, Reddick has steadfastly refused to compromise on the firm's commitment to personal attention to each client's case. This attention to detail along with a highly talented, experienced team of attorneys and support staff has garnered national success and recognition. Brian Reddick has consistently won multi-million-dollar verdicts the course of his career. Moreover, Reddick has obtained over a billion dollars in combined settlements and verdicts for his clients.

With a license to practice law in Arkansas, Colorado, Kentucky, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Mexico, New York, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, West Virginia, Mr. Reddick delivers legal solutions and results throughout the United States.

In addition to big verdicts, big settlements in cases across the country, Mr. Reddick has also been awarded an "AV rating" by Martindale Hubbell, the highest rating an attorney can achieve in both legal ability and ethical standards.

Mr. Reddick is a member of the National Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice. He was selected to receive America's Top 100 Lifetime Achievement Award, has also been named a Super Lawyer in each consecutive year since 2012, was appointed Champion for Justice by his Arkansas legal peers twice, was selected by his peers for membership in the American Board of Trial Advocates, and has received numerous other prestigious awards for his service.

Of all of his accomplishments, Mr. Reddick is most proud of his family. Family, friends and faith have provided the bedrock for all of Reddick's accomplishments. To that end, Brian is fond of saying, "It is vitally important to me that my family is proud of what I do for our clients."

attorneys.name: Connor Reddick
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Neglect Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Connor wears several different hats at Reddick Law PLLC. Primarily focusing on the client intake and pre-litigation workup side of nursing home cases, he also oversees the firm's general personal injury practice, is involved with mass torts, and manages the firm's marketing department. Connor is licensed to practice law in Arkansas, Colorado, Missouri and New Mexico.

Born and raised in Arkansas, Connor attended high school at Episcopal Collegiate School in Little Rock before moving to Fayetteville for college. After graduating from the University of Arkansas with his bachelor's degree, Connor attended the William H. Bowen School of Law in Little Rock and obtained his juris doctrate in May of 2020. While in law school, Connor earned Top Paper awards in his Health Law and Law & Medicine classes.

Outside of work, Connor enjoys spending his time outdoors, attending Razorback games, exercising, and traveling. An avid duck hunter, Connor and his British Labrador Retriever, Lincoln, frequent the flooded timber of Stuttgart, AR during the winter months. Above all else, Connor cherishes his time with his family members and friends for, without them, he would not be the person that he is today.

The law has held a special place in Connor's heart for as long as he can remember. Connor credits his father, Brian Reddick, founder of Reddick Law PLLC, for exposing him to the legal profession at a young age. Through being raised by an attorney, Connor quickly developed a passion for representing those who have been hurt or wronged and have nowhere else to turn. Possessing the ability to make a positive difference in the lives of his clients is a privilege that Connor values most in his life, and one that serves as his biggest source of motivation to work hard each and every day.

attorneys.name: Landon Reeves
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Corporate Law Lawyers in Batesville, AR
attorneys.bio:
Landon was born and raised in Batesville, Arkansas, and he is very proud to call Batesville his hometown. Before founding Reeves Law Firm, Landon practiced in Little Rock, Arkansas, with one of the largest national law firms in Arkansas where he regularly worked with some of the largest corporations in Arkansas as well as small and medium-sized companies. His experience working on large scale transactions, including mergers, acquisitions, and other strategic transactions, as well as all matters related to corporate governance and business development, is what sets him apart in Batesville and the region.

Landon’s practice includes the representation of individuals and businesses in matters involving business and corporate law, business and commercial litigation, estate planning, estate litigation, personal injury law, and probate and estate administration.

Landon is very proud of his academic achievements during law school where he graduated Magna Cum Laude, with Honors, and in the top 14% of his class. During law school, he served on the Editorial Board of the Law Review at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock – William H. Bowen School of Law where his article analyzing specific patent law was published in 2015.

Prior to attending law school, Landon worked in the oil and gas industry for over 6 years with such major corporations as Schlumberger, Baker Hughes, and Southwestern Energy focusing on wireline field engineering, production fluid chemistry, and environmental analysis. Landon earned a degree in Biology from Hendrix College in 2006.

Landon is a member of the Batesville City Council, a board member of the Batesville Area Chamber of Commerce, a member of the Batesville Kiwanis Club, Chairman of the Batesville-Independence County Industrial Development Corporation, a Board of Director of Vital Link, Inc., and a Board of Director of the Old Independence Regional Museum.

attorneys.name: Wesley Rhodes
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
With over eight years of experience defending clients in Little Rock and across Pulaski County, Wesley Rhodes has built a reputation as a fierce and strategic criminal defense attorney who combines courtroom experience with modern technology to deliver efficient, high-quality representation. Whether facing DUI charges, drug offenses, domestic battery, theft, or more serious felonies, Wesley is committed to protecting his clients’ rights and freedom at every stage of the legal process.

Born and raised in Arkansas, Wesley understands not just the law, but the communities, courts, and people he serves. He has spent his career navigating the unique challenges of the local legal system — from Pulaski County District Court to Circuit Courts all over Arkansas — giving him an insider’s perspective that few attorneys can match.

Wesley’s approach to criminal defense is personal, proactive, and client-focused. He believes every case deserves a tailored strategy, and he works closely with clients to understand their situation, explain their options clearly, and prepare for the best possible outcome. He’s known for his calm, strategic presence in the courtroom, his ability to read the room, and his unwavering commitment to his clients’ rights.

In addition to traditional legal skills, Wesley leverages modern tools and technology to stay ahead of the curve. From case management and legal research to motion drafting and trial preparation, he uses AI-assisted tools and efficient workflows to maximize results while minimizing unnecessary stress for his clients.

Outside the courtroom, Wesley is deeply involved in the Arkansas legal community, staying current on changes in criminal law and court procedures. He is passionate about mentoring young lawyers and ensuring access to high-quality legal defense for all members of the community.

If you’re facing criminal charges in Little Rock, Pulaski County, or anywhere in Arkansas — Wesley Rhodes offers the experience, strategy, and local insight to defend your rights aggressively and effectively.

Call today for a confidential consultation — your freedom deserves dedicated, experienced advocacy.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
I am a child of divorced parents, a second wife, a step-mom, and a mom. Those roles influence and enhance my family law representation every single day. I also know how it feels to be a client, having watched my husband go through a custody battle for his daughter when she was very young. I will never forget that feeling of vulnerability, hope, and dependence on the attorney to keep us informed and to fight for what was important to us. Now, years later, as my stepdaughter has developed into a wonderful, well-adjusted adult, I am grateful for the way we all ultimately raised her to love every person in her family, not just "our side."

My parents were a role model for that version of a split family. Although they were often separated and then divorced during my childhood, they never put us in the middle of their conflicts. Through my childhood, they attended and sat together at our basketball games, pageants, awards ceremonies; and through my dad's passing in 2018, they were both present at the Thanksgiving table and to at Christmas; and they never spoke ill of each other in front of us. I use all of these experiences to help my clients navigate what is often the one of the worst experiences of their life--separating from their significant other and fighting for their rights to their children, property, and livelihood. As I have reached middle age, I have a keen appreciation for the importance of preserving my clients' property and financial stability, in the wake of divorce.

And although the laws and caselaw have finally begun to catch up to legislating correctly, I am proud to say that I have always fought hard for my LGBTQ+ clients--whether it's related to their parental rights or their property. We are a safe space for these clients, having been the law firm that prevailed in first establishing court-ordered visitation rights for a non-biological parent. Family law is my passion. I love knowing that my work has made a difference in my clients' lives, that I have helped them make a new start, and in being here for them if and when they need help in the future.

attorneys.name: Catherine A. Ryan
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Little Rock native Catherine Ryan joined Dodds, Kidd & Ryan in 2016 after fourteen years representing injured parties as a trial lawyer in Boston, Massachusetts. Catherine practices in all areas of civil litigation, with an emphasis in tort and product liability and professional negligence claims. She has successfully brought appeals of both civil and criminal matters to the Arkansas Supreme Court and Court of Appeals. Catherine was elected to become a Member of the Fellows of the American Bar Foundation, an organization of legal professionals that is limited to the top one percent of lawyers licensed to practice in each jurisdiction. She has successfully represented clients in state and Federal court on a wide-variety of cases ranging from simple auto accidents to contract disputes, multi-district litigation and qui-tam claims.

Catherine has obtained and successfully defended against summary judgment dismissal of a variety of claims including legal malpractice, breach of contract, negligent design and negligent entrustment in both state and Federal court. Catherine successfully defended appeals of lower court victories, including a judgment after a jury’s verdict in her client’s favor for $973,000. Catherine served on the Board of Governors of the Massachusetts Academy of Trial Attorneys, lectures on various topics and is a co-author of the Emotional Distress chapter of the Massachusetts Tort Law Manual. She was recognized as a “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers publication in 2010, 2011, 2012, and 2013.

Catherine is licensed to practice in the State of Arkansas, as well as the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts and the 1st Circuit Court of Appeals. She is a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation and a member of the Arkansas Bar Association, the American Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the Massachusetts Academy of Trial Attorneys and the Massachusetts Bar Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Conway, AR
attorneys.bio:
Landon T. Sanders graduated from Conway High School in Conway, Arkansas. He earned his degree in social studies education from the University of Central Arkansas, where he graduated Summa Cum Laude. Landon graduated Cum Laude from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock William H. Bowen School of Law.

Throughout school and after graduation, Landon gained invaluable experience in Arkansas courtrooms. He clerked through an externship program for an Arkansas Court of Appeals Judge, clerked for the governor’s office during the 2015 legislative session, and served as a prosecutor for more than a year. He’s briefed the governor on bills introduced by legislature, handled issues regarding pardons and gun rights in the Arkansas Clemency & Extraditions office, and worked through felony and misdemeanor cases in central Arkansas. Previously, Landon served as a deputy prosecuting attorney for the Fifteenth Judicial District of Arkansas, where he handled criminal matters in Circuit and District Court.

Now, Landon focuses on criminal law, including misdemeanors and felonies - from traffic tickets to serious felonies. Landon is prepared through his past experience to take a case to trial.

Preston T. Sanders graduated from the University of Central Arkansas where he gained a degree in Economics, with a focus in International Trade. Preston received his law degree from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock William H. Bowen School of Law, where he graduated Cum Laude.

Preston grew up in Conway, Arkansas, where he went on to establish The Sanders Firm PLLC in 2016 with his brother and partner, Landon T. Sanders. He began as an eager pupil of the law while studying at UCA, and served as the firm’s notary public and office manager. He utilized the skills he learned at UCA as an economics major to help transform The Sanders Firm into what it is today.

During his time at The Sanders Firm, Preston developed a particular interest in Criminal Defense and focused his studies during school to further that interest. He has since continued that pursuit, serving as special prosecutor, and traveling the greater part of the State of Arkansas for trial practice. Throughout this time, he has gained invaluable experience and attended advanced training across the country.

Preston understands that each and every client is unique. He is goal-oriented and enjoys tailoring his work to the particular client and matter at hand so that each client’s expectations are fully satisfied, and the best possible outcome under the circumstances is achieved.

attorneys.name: Scott A. Scholl
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
From an early age, I found that I was very adept at working with fine details and applying them toward a solution. As someone who has always been an analytical thinker, I reveled in the art of critical thinking and problem-solving. This is what eventually led to me joining the U.S. Army.

I joined the Army so that I could learn to further develop those skills and apply them to real-world situations. For me, one of the best parts of serving was learning to work with others toward a common goal. It's what not only led me toward serving my country, but also a big part of what got me through my service, which included my participation in the invasion of Panama in 1989.

From the Military to the Legal Profession

When I finished my service, I was immediately drawn toward practicing law because I knew it would allow me to continue to use my analytical and problem-solving skills to serve my community. I was quickly accepted into the University of Nebraska College of Law and received my Juris Doctor before returning to my home state of Arkansas to begin practicing law. From the outset, I decided to focus on a few areas of the law that would provide me with the opportunity to help people who often didn't have the means or opportunity to help themselves.

"I know what it's like to be faced with overwhelming challenges. That's why I make it my job to help others through tough situations."

My initial focus was on legal appeals because I knew that my ability to study the smallest details of a case could go a long way toward helping my clients reverse the original decision in their case. Outside of appeals, I decided to also devote my knowledge and expertise toward family and military law.

Given my military background and my familiarity with many of the legal entanglements associated with military service, I knew I wanted to provide counsel and support for the brave men and women who have served and continue to serve this great country. Serving in the U.S. Army has provided me with a strong familiarity with the unique situations that service members face, both in regards to their relationships with family and their legal affairs.

Legal Services You Can Trust

At the end of the day, my goal is to provide affordable, reliable legal services and representation to individuals and families in Little Rock, Conway, and across the state of Arkansas. With over two decades of experience practicing law throughout the state, I'm truly committed to helping the members of my community navigate the legal system. I do this by providing effective legal strategies that can help them overcome whatever challenges they may be facing.

Through compassion, dedication, and a relentless work ethic, I'll do everything I can to help my clients find a solution that can help them move forward. So if you or someone you know is looking for trusted legal counsel, call my office today and schedule a free case consultation.

attorneys.name: Bob Sexton
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Bob Sexton has been practicing law in Arkansas for over 20 years. A product of the small town of Lonoke, Sexton has lived in Arkansas his entire life. He attended college at Ouachita Baptist University in Arkadelphia and then moved to the capital city to attend the Bowen School of Law at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock.

Sexton began working with Mike Rainwater in the 1990’s and together with Stephen Holt they formed Rainwater, Holt & Sexton in 2006. As a partner at the largest personal injury law firm in Arkansas, Sexton has helped oversee tremendous growth. What started as a handful of attorneys and staff has now grown to over 30 attorneys and 100+ support staff. “We’re big enough to go against any insurance company, but we’re small enough to care about the clients,” said Sexton. The growth has been possible because of the excellence and care with which they have served thousands of clients. “I count it a great honor to represent the people of Arkansas,” said Sexton. “I genuinely like talking to and helping people, and I’m grateful we have helped so many Arkansans throughout the years.”

The law energizes Sexton. He loves being presented a difficult and problematic situation and making it work for the client. Throughout his career he has done this for the thousands of clients he has represented. What guides him in the difficult situations is pretty easy, “…it’s fairness” he says, “People in Arkansas want to be treated fairly. Rainwater, Holt & Sexton provides them with a pathway to solve their problems.”

While the law is important to Sexton, his family also plays a huge role in his life. He is married to his college sweetheart and they have 3 children. When he is not working, Sexton is with his family and enjoying Arkansas outdoors. He is an avid duck hunter and also enjoys fishing in the warmer months. “I decided early on that if my children were going to learn to hunt and fish, they were going to learn it from me,” said Sexton. “So I love being in a duck blind with my kids as the sun starts peaking over the horizon or showing them how to fish on one of the many great rivers we have in the state,” he added.

Sexton is also very involved at his church and in the community. He is a board member for the Fellowship of Christian Athletes, the William H. Bowen School of Law Alumni Association, the Ouachita Baptist University Higginbotham School of Business, and on the Board of Governors for the Arkansas Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.bio:
Jessica Smith is a native Arkansan who grew up in Glen Rose, Arkansas, a small town in Hot Spring County. After graduating from Glen Rose High School, she received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock. After obtaining her degree, Smith worked as a corporate paralegal at Windstream Communications in Little Rock and ABF Freight in Fort Smith.

During her time as a paralegal, Smith witnessed the justice that our legal system can provide to individuals who have been wronged and quickly realized she wanted to play an active role in that process by becoming an attorney. As such, Smith then attended law school as a Dean’s Fellow at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock William H. Bowen School of Law, where she received her Juris Doctorate.

attorneys.name: D. Kimbro Stephens Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Long-term Care Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
D. Kimbro Stephens had big dreams as a teenager growing up in Conway, Arkansas. The son of a pioneer in the medical field and a well-known football coach, Kimbro knew he wanted, like his parents, to help others. He had no idea that a career in elder law would be the way. But since he graduated from Harvard University cum laude with a degree in economics and then a Juris Doctorate from the University of Arkansas School of Law, he found his way to health care then to elder law. Kimbro’s parents were the late Wanda Ward Stephens, M.D., an early female medical student who would become a leading psychiatrist in the state and head football coach Ken Stephens who is an Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame inductee. Both of his parents taught him the importance of investing in others with his mother’s advice, “It’s not what you say but how you say it.” Kimbro has never forgotten that principle.

After receiving his law degree in 1988 where he graduated with honors and was a member of the Arkansas Law Review and served as National Student Officer of the Delta Theta Phi Law fraternity, Kimbro assisted his mother in opening a first-of-its-kind Christian psychiatric hospital in Arkansas, Living Hope Institute. He worked for more than 20 years in hospital administration and executive healthcare management. During that time, he found a passion for helping people in crisis. As a healthcare executive, Kimbro established many programs for the delivery of medical services and served in many capacities including CEO and General Counsel. This is where he began using his gifted problem-solving skills for families to navigate the red tape of the insurance industry that is often at odds with patient needs and financial situations. We all know it is an intimidating and frightening experience to traverse the healthcare maze as the costs often exceed a family’s resources.

Then in a pain-to-purpose scenario, Kimbro had to walk that same path when dealing with the disabling and terminal health issues with his mother’s liver cancer diagnosis in 2009. The 19 months that followed had Kimbro learn to advocate for his helpless mother but also had him witness a chain of events that no family should experience. Kimbro opened his private law practice dedicated to helping seniors find workable solutions so they can get the quality care they need and want without going through financial devastation in the process.

Now he brings his wealth of experience to the Jurist Law Group as Co-Founder in 2015 and serves as Managing Attorney, where he devotedly guides families in the daunting maze of long-term care and helps them with asset protection and estate planning. Kimbro has learned that all families need this type of service; it is not for just the wealthy families but for all families trying to protect their family’s assets.

attorneys.name: Matthew D. Swindle
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Matthew D. Swindle graduated summa cum laude from Harding University in 2007. Mr. Swindle then accepted a fellowship to study law at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock. While in law school, he was recognized for outstanding performance in multiple subject areas including legal research, writing & advocacy, evidence, and ethics. He was also selected by the American Bar Association for the Janet D. Steiger fellowship, through which Mr. Swindle worked with the Consumer Protection Division of the Arkansas Attorney General's office where he researched consumer issues and worked to protect Arkansans through enforcement of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

In 2012, Mr. Swindle graduated from law school with a High Honors designation and was ranked number one in his class. He then began his practice of law with Reddick Law PLLC, where he handled appeals, class action litigation, and individual cases of nursing home abuse and malpractice. In 2015, Mr. Swindle accepted an appointment to clerk at the Arkansas Supreme Court for Justice Rhonda K. Wood. In 2016, he joined the faculty of Harding University where he attained the rank of Associate Professor of Criminal Justice and served as an advisor. While teaching at Harding, Mr. Swindle taught Introduction to Criminal Justice, Criminal Law, Drugs, Alcohol & Crime, Evidence, Criminal Procedure, and Professional Ethics. During his time teaching, Mr. Swindle maintained a practice of counsel with Reddick Law PLLC, in which he handled appeals, consulted on novel legal issues and class action and medical malpractice litigation, as well as represented Arkansas's cities and counties in their case against opioid manufacturers and distributors.

In July 2022, Mr. Swindle returned to full-time practice with Reddick Law PLLC. As part of his practice, he most frequently litigates cases involving nursing home abuse and neglect and assisted living facility abuse and neglect. He also handles a number of the firm's appeals, and has worked on class actions, civil rights cases, and deceptive trade practices cases.

attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Jessica Bass Vaught has had the privilege of practicing law with Rainwater, Holt & Sexton since 2008. She grew up in the small, south Arkansas town of Arkadelphia and received a B.A. in Political Science from Baylor University in Waco, Texas. She then returned home to Arkansas to attend UALR’s Bowen School of Law.

Jessica enjoys representing Rainwater, Holt & Sexton clients and advocating for the best outcome in each client’s case. Without question, the firm’s caring commitment to its clients and communities across Arkansas sets it apart.

Jessica’s primary practice area is bankruptcy, and she participates in the Central Arkansas Debtor-Creditor Bar. She is also a member of the Arkansas Association of Women Lawyers, the Arkansas Bar Association, and the Pulaski County Bar Association, and recently served on the Arkansas Bar Association’s Commission on Diversity. She is an adjunct professor at the UALR Bowen School of Law, where she has taught Law and Literature and Remedies.

Jessica and her husband, L.B., enjoy volunteering with their church and their teenage children’s activities. Jessica is especially grateful for the family-friendly focus encouraged by Rainwater, Holt & Sexton. From firm-sponsored Travelers baseball game outings to fall family picnics and community outreach opportunities, the firm fosters fellowship and fun.

The firm’s team-based approach and effective working relationships among employees ensure that our clients receive superior service consistently. Rainwater, Holt & Sexton’s emphasis on community-focused initiatives, such as our monthly charitable giving program, encourages consideration of others and collective contribution to something larger than ourselves.

Jessica Bass Vaught is thankful and proud to be a part of Rainwater, Holt & Sexton.

attorneys.name: Robert T. Veon
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Texarkana, AR
attorneys.bio:
Robert T. Veon received his Bachelor of Arts degree from Grove City College in Grove City, Pennsylvania (1986). He was awarded the Juris Doctor degree from The University of Arkansas School of Law in Fayetteville, Arkansas (1990). Mr. Veon is admitted to practice before the state courts in Arkansas, Texas, Pennsylvania and Missouri. He is admitted to The United States District Courts for the Eastern/Western Districts of Arkansas, Eastern District of Texas, Northern District of Texas, Southern District of Texas, Eastern and Middle Districts of Pennsylvania as well as the United States Courts of Appeals for the 8th, 5th and 3rd Circuits.

Mr. Veon is a member of The International Association of Defense Counsel (Defense Law Journal Board of Editors), Defense Research Institute (Chair, Young Lawyers Committee 2000/2001, Pennsylvania State Representative 2000-2003) and former member of The Pennsylvania Defense Institute (Chair, Young Members Committee 1998) and Philadelphia Association of Defense Counsel (Executive Board- elected to 2 terms). He is a member of the Arkansas Bar Association, Arkansas Association of Defense Counsel, State Bar of Texas, Texas Association of Defense Counsel and the American Bar Association.

Mr. Veon has secured successful verdicts as a defense trial attorney in both state and Federal courts. In addition to an active commercial practice representing Fortune 100 and 500 companies, he represents corporations, individuals, insureds and self-insured entities in the defense of product liability, transportation, premises, dram shop, automobile negligence, uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage and insurance coverage/bad faith. Mr. Veon has experience in professional liability cases, including medical malpractice and the defense of institutions providing long term care.

Mr. Veon has served as faculty at programs presented by the National Institute for Trial Advocacy, the Defense Research Institute, the Pennsylvania Defense Institute, the Philadelphia Association of Defense Counsel, the National Business Institute, the International Association of Defense Counsel and has served as Adjunct Faculty for the Trial Advocacy Training Program at Louisiana State University School of Law. Mr. Veon is AV rated by Martindale Hubbell. He is the resident shareholder in the Arkansas/Texas office of McDonald Veon P.A.

attorneys.name: Lloyd Warford
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse and Neglect Litigation Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Lloyd Warford began his career in 1988 as a deputy prosecuting attorney in Pulaski County, where he served as the Division Chief of the Prosecutors’ Drug Prosecution Unit and later the Division Chief of the Prosecutor's Gang Prosecution Unit. In the years since he left the prosecutor’s Office, he has served the people of this state as the Assistant Director of the State’s Division of Youth Services, as an Attorney with the Department of Human Services, a Pulaski County Public Defender, and from January 2015 until 2023 as a Deputy Attorney General and Director of the Arkansas Medicaid Fraud Control Unit.

The Arkansas Medicaid Fraud Control Unit includes two investigative and prosecution teams: the Medicaid Fraud and Elder Protection teams. The Elder Protection Team is responsible for prosecuting abuse, neglect, and exploitation in long term care facilities and for enforcing the civil maltreatment statutes of the state of Arkansas. Under Lloyd’s leadership, the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit obtained 203 convictions and 191 civil settlements, with court orders and settlements totaling more than 81 million dollars.

Lloyd has been a leader throughout his career. Lloyd served as chairman of the Drug Control Committee of the Arkansas Prosecuting Attorneys Association. He was elected and served on the Board of Directors of the Arkansas Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and nationally on the Executive Committee of the National Association of Medicaid Fraud Control Units.

As an attorney at Reddick Law PLLC, he now focuses on nursing home abuse and neglect litigation, representing his clients and their families in all stages of the litigation and arbitration processes.

Lloyd is proud to be a military dependent (Air Force Brat) and loves military history. Lloyd’s father is a Vietnam veteran and retired Air Force officer. Lloyd’s grandfather was a World War II veteran and a First Special Services Force member. He is proud to have served ten years in the Army Reserves. He loves deer hunting, and he and his wife, Mandy Weir Warford, are avid musical theater fans and do what they can to help support several local community theaters. Lloyd is blessed to have three children and four grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Eric Wewers
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse and Neglect Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Eric Wewers graduated from the UALR School of Law in 1990. After graduation, he moved to Dallas, Texas, and began working for the prestigious firm of DeHay & Blanchard. There, he worked under the guidance of Carlyle DeHay and Gary Elliston. In 1992, Wewers left DeHay & Blanchard to form the law firm of DeHay & Elliston. During this time, he tried cases in Dallas, Corpus Christi, San Antonio, El Paso, Waco, Austin, and Houston. On January 1, 2001, Wewers resigned from the partnership of DeHay & Elliston to open the Texas office for the nationally known firm of Wilkes & McHugh, representing victims of nursing home abuse and neglect. His areas of practice focused on representing those victims of nursing home abuse and neglect in both Texas and Arkansas. In October 2002, Wilkes & McHugh moved Wewers back home to Little Rock to work in their office here. There, he was responsible for cases in both Arkansas and Texas. On November 1, 2003, The Law Offices of Eric D. Wewers was formed. Since 2008, Wewers has also served as General Counsel for St. Joseph Helpers and became General Counsel for Arkansas Right to Life at the recommendation of Judge Leon Holmes when he took the bench in 2004. In early 2014, Wewers started working as of counsel with ReddickMoss, where he focused his practice on nursing home abuse and neglect cases.

At Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, Wewers continues to work for victims of nursing home abuse and neglect. In his career, Wewers has had settlements totaling over $25 million.

attorneys.name: Robbie White
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Robbie White, a lifelong Arkansan, grew up on a farm in Highfill, Arkansas. He graduated as a salutatorian from Gentry High School. After high school, he attended Hendrix College in Conway, where he played varsity soccer. He then transferred to the University of Arkansas at Fayetteville, where he earned his bachelor’s degree in sociology and criminal justice, followed by his law degree from the University of Arkansas School of Law.

During law school, White had the opportunity to clerk at the Odom Law Firm in Fayetteville, where he developed a passion for helping clients with their personal injury cases. He continued pursuing his passion for helping injured clients at Taylor King Law, where he gained valuable courtroom experience working as a litigation attorney.

White decided to become an attorney because he wanted to be a leader in his community and a valuable resource for people when they are in need. Over the years, White has developed expertise in helping clients who have been injured because of the negligence of others, and he is excited to continue advocating for those who are suffering life-changing trauma here at Rainwater, Holt & Sexton.

In his free time, White enjoys playing golf, going to the Razorback game, hunting, fishing, and spending time with his wife, Kara, daughter Vivian, and sons Nolan and Simon.

attorneys.name: Wade A. Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Eureka Springs, AR
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Farmington, Wade Williams is a graduate of Fayetteville High School. Mr. Williams graduated from the University of Arkansas in 1987 with a Bachelor of Science degree in agricultural business. He graduated from the University of Arkansas School of Law Fayetteville in 1990, and was admitted to the Arkansas Bar that same year.

From law school, Mr. Williams went to work for Attorney Larry Garrett in Bentonville. He also opened a legal office with Garrett in Holiday Island in 1990. In 1992, Mr. Williams purchased Bromstad Abstract and Title Co. in Eureka Springs. He ran the title company and practiced law from there until 1997, when he opened a sole practitioner law practice in Holiday Island.

He sold the title company in 2002, opened a satellite law office in Farmington in 2003, and bought an interest in Kings River Title Co. in 2006.

In 2006, he also moved his office from Holiday Island to its present location in historic downtown Eureka Springs. He lives in Fayetteville and splits his time between his two offices.

He is a member of Carroll County Bar Association, Arkansas Bar Association, American Bar Association, and is licensed to practice in federal district court. Mr. Williams is also a member of the Arkansas and American Land Title Associations, and is chairman of the Carroll Health Foundation planned giving committee. He is a member of the Holiday Island Chamber of Commerce, Eureka Springs Chamber of Commerce, and the Farmington Chamber of Commerce.

Mr. Williams was appointed by Gov. Mike Huckabee to serve on the State Parks, Recreation and Travel Commission in 1997 and reappointed in 2001. He now serves on The Natural Heritage Commission, which Gov. Mike Beebe appointed Mr. Williams to in 2009. He also serves on Board of Directors of the First National Bank of Berryville.

Practice Areas

Wade Williams provides experienced legal representation throughout Arkansas in the following areas of practice:

Small business formation (corporations, LLCs, partnerships)

Business transactions

Estate planning trusts, wills, guardianships

Real Estate transactions, boundary disputes, quiet titles

Collections and recovery of personal property

Foreclosures

Contract Agreements prenuptial, employment, easements, business, real estate Probate

Mr. Williams represents clients throughout Arkansas, including Eureka Springs, Berryville, Fayetteville, Springdale, Rogers, Bentonville, Fort Smith, Harrison, Mountain Home, and Little Rock. He is admitted to practice before all Arkansas State and Federal courts.

attorneys.name: Victor D. "Trey" Wright III
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Since 2001 Victor D. Trey Wright III has been practicing law in Little Rock, Arkansas. Trey is licensed to practice in Arkansas State Courts, Arkansas Court of Appeals, the Supreme Court of Arkansas and United States District Courts, Trey has the experience and background necessary to successfully and competently represent you anywhere in the State of Arkansas. Trey's home area encompasses Pulaski, Lonoke, Faulkner, and Saline County, where he tries cases in Little Rock, North Little Rock, Bryant, Benton, Lonoke, Cabot, and Conway.

In 2004, Trey opened the Wright Law Firm. The Wright Law Firm focuses on trial related work in the following areas: Family Law, which includes divorce, child custody, child support, adoptions, visitation rights, and grandparent visitation rights. Prior to founding the Wright Law Firm, Trey worked for the James Law Firm for 7 years serving as a law clerk, associate, and finally as a senior associate.

Trey is a trial lawyer in the truest sense of the word. Trey has tried many cases throughout the state ranging from matters as small as parking tickets to Capital Murder trials. This extensive trial experience before judges and juries all around Arkansas has helped Trey become a strong and effective advocate for his clients.

Throughout the years Trey has shown himself to be a competent and capable attorney and, has been asked to serve as a Special judge when the sitting judges are unavailable hear a case.

Trey received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock William H. Bowen School of Law in 2001. In 1998, he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in History from Arkansas State University, and is a 1994 graduate of Catholic High School in Little Rock.

Trey is a member of the Arkansas Bar Association, the Pulaski County Bar Association, the Lonoke County Bar Association, the Arkansas Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys, and the Arkansas Trial Lawyers Association. Membership in these organizations ensures that Trey stays up to date on the latest trends and developments in the law.

Trey is currently serving in the House of Delegates for the Arkansas Bar Association where he works to determine the policies and procedures of the Bar as well as propose the changes in laws for the state legislature to review. As a member of the bar, Trey co-authored the 18 and Life to Go, a Handbook for Young Arkansas, and was responsible for the child custody section of the handbook.

attorneys.name: James W. "Jim" Wyatt
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Jim is a life long Arkansan. Born in Searcy, Arkansas, Jim moved to North Little Rock, Arkansas in 1983, where he graduated from North Little Rock Northeast High School. After graduating college from the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville, Jim moved back to Little Rock to attend the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (Bowen) School of Law. After law school, Jim moved back to North Little Rock where he raised his two children. When not practing law, Jim enjoys hunting, fishing, playing golf and kayaking the Buffalo River.

Jim has argued before the Arkansas Supreme Court and the United States Court of Appeals, Eight Circuit. He has served as special judge in Pulaski County District Courts as well as Pulaski County Circuit Court. He has been a Continuing Legal Education (CLE) speaker at numerous criminal law seminars, and serves as lead attorney on capital murder death penalty cases, as well as all other felony cases across the state of Arkansas. In addition to his state court practice, Jim also practices in federal court, where he has handled a wide range of federal criminal cases, including drug cases, white collar fraud, federal health care fraud and murder.

attorneys.name: Laura Beth York
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Little Rock, AR
attorneys.bio:
Laura Beth York moved to Arkansas when she was 10 years old. She grew up in Conway, Arkansas, and was fortunate enough to attend Hendrix College in her hometown. She stayed in Arkansas and obtained her law degree from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock School of Law. Following graduation, she took a chance and moved to South Carolina with her husband, where she worked as an attorney at Legal Aid for almost two years before the opportunity arose for her and her husband to move back to Arkansas.

Laura Beth knew that she wanted to practice in the area of workers’ compensation when her father was injured at work. It was a career-ending injury, and it was her first year of law school. It was a life-changing moment for her and her family. When she moved back to Arkansas, she immediately went to work at the Arkansas Workers’ Compensation Commission, writing opinions at the Full Commission.

Helping injured workers is not only a passion for Laura Beth, but also keeps her rooted in an area of the law that needs personal understanding about what each claimant experiences. Laura Beth knew that by choosing to work at Rainwater, Holt & Sexton, she would be able to not only help injured workers’ navigate the waters of the workers’ compensation system, but she would also be able to help them by utilizing the legal resources that a larger firm can offer, such as advice on Social Security Disability, Bankruptcy, or whether their claim falls outside of the workers’ compensation system.

In her spare time, Laura Beth is an active member of her church, Christ the King Catholic Church in Little Rock, Arkansas. She enjoys going on adventures with her husband and two children, including hiking, kayaking, and golfing. Of course, Saturdays in the Fall are reserved for cheering on the Arkansas Razorbacks!

attorneys.bio:
A native of Pargould, Arkansas, Heather Zachary attended Hendrix College in Conway, Arkansas, as a Distinguished Governor's Scholar, and graduated cum laude with a bachelor's degree in Psychology in 2001. Ms. Zachary then attended law school at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. She was a member of the Georgetown Journal of Law and Policy and was recognized for academic excellence in Evidence before earning her J.D. in 2004.

Prior to returning to Arkansas, Ms. Zachary worked in the Washington, D.C. office of McDermott Will & Emery, a premier international law firm. Ms. Zachary then served two years working at the Arkansas Supreme Court as a law clerk for the Honorable Justice Annabelle Imber Tuck. Ms. Zachary then accepted a position at Chisenhall, Nestrud & Julian, where she focused her practice on environmental and employment law, as well as appeals. In 2014, Ms. Zachary returned to the Arkansas Supreme Court, where she clerked for the Honorable Justice Courtney Hudson until 2016, at which point Ms. Zachary joined Williams & Anderson. During her tenure at Williams & Anderson, Ms. Zachary handled appeals and class action litigation. She then joined Reddick Law PLLC, where she focuses on appeals, nursing home abuse, and other complex personal injury litigation.

Ms. Zachary is admitted to practice before the following courts:

The Supreme Court of the United States

The Arkansas Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Arkansas

United States District Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Arkansas

The Tennessee Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Tennessee

The Oklahoma Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Oklahoma

The Missouri Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Missouri (application approved; admission pending)

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
A native of Pargould, Arkansas, Heather Zachary attended Hendrix College in Conway, Arkansas, as a Distinguished Governor's Scholar, and graduated cum laude with a bachelor's degree in Psychology in 2001. Ms. Zachary then attended law school at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. She was a member of the Georgetown Journal of Law and Policy and was recognized for academic excellence in Evidence before earning her J.D. in 2004.

Prior to returning to Arkansas, Ms. Zachary worked in the Washington, D.C. office of McDermott Will & Emery, a premier international law firm. Ms. Zachary then served two years working at the Arkansas Supreme Court as a law clerk for the Honorable Justice Annabelle Imber Tuck. Ms. Zachary then accepted a position at Chisenhall, Nestrud & Julian, where she focused her practice on environmental and employment law, as well as appeals. In 2014, Ms. Zachary returned to the Arkansas Supreme Court, where she clerked for the Honorable Justice Courtney Hudson until 2016, at which point Ms. Zachary joined Williams & Anderson. During her tenure at Williams & Anderson, Ms. Zachary handled appeals and class action litigation. She then joined Reddick Law PLLC, where she focuses on appeals, nursing home abuse, and other complex personal injury litigation.

Ms. Zachary is admitted to practice before the following courts:

The Supreme Court of the United States

The Arkansas Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Arkansas

United States District Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Arkansas

The Tennessee Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Tennessee

The Oklahoma Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Oklahoma

The Missouri Supreme Court and all inferior courts in the State of Missouri (application approved; admission pending)
